sections.h2: Who records deeds in Gallia County
sections.html:
The Gallia County Recorder in Gallipolis records deeds, mortgages, leases, land contracts, liens and plats for the county. Ohio's first legislature had judges appoint a recorder in each county, the post became elective in 1829, and the term was fixed at four years in 1936.

Gallia County dates to March 25, 1803, and runs along the Ohio River where Ohio meets West Virginia. Gallipolis is the seat, with Cheshire, Crown City, Rio Grande, Centerville and Vinton as the other villages, and every one of them files into the same land records. A sale in any of those villages follows the same path through the Auditor and then the Recorder.

The Recorder is at 18 Locust Street, Gallipolis, Ohio 45631. Weekday hours run eight to four. Call 740-446-4612 and ask for extension 1247, 1248 or 1329.

  • County Auditor: same address, Room 1264, with the real estate desk on extension 1201.
  • Recorder's property search: an online index of recorded documents.
  • Auditor's parcel search, GIS parcel viewer, sales reports and delinquency reports: available from the Auditor's website.

Looking at the land records costs nothing. Public access is free, so a buyer, a title agent or you can review the index before closing.

A deed must be transferred in the Auditor's office before it is recorded, so the Auditor is your first stop.

The Auditor's website posts a conveyance fee calculator and a tax estimator under Tools, with the statement of value form for the conveyance fee among its forms. The statewide piece of the conveyance fee is a dollar, or ten cents per hundred dollars of value if that is larger (R.C. 319.54(G)(3)). A county board may stack a tax of up to thirty cents per hundred on top (R.C. 322.02). Use the Auditor's calculator for Gallia County's total, and ask the real estate desk about exemptions such as a transfer with no money or other consideration.

The county has more than 29,000 parcels and more than 2,500 manufactured and mobile homes. A Community Reinvestment Area began on December 2, 2024, so ask the Auditor what that program covers for your parcel.

sections.h2: What the Recorder requires on a deed
sections.html:
The Recorder publishes a checklist, and a deed or mortgage that misses an item comes back. The list includes:

  • a full legal description naming the township or city, lot or subdivision and acreage;
  • grantor names spelled exactly as they are signed and notarized;
  • the permanent parcel number wherever the real estate is described;
  • a notary signature, seal and expiration date;
  • a "prepared by" line, which Ohio requires;
  • names typed beneath the original signatures;
  • a stamped, addressed return envelope big enough to hold the papers.

Deputies cannot fix a lot number or other typo. Whoever made the document must make the change. Documents boxed for pickup must be claimed within a week or they are mailed out at the box holder's cost.

State rules put a deed at $34 for pages one and two and $8 for every later page, with an optional county preservation surcharge of up to $5. Gallia posts $39.00 for the opening two pages and $8.00 for each later page. The state splits each of its fees evenly with the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

Selected Gallia County Recorder charges
Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage, lease, affidavit, certificate of transfer$39.00 first two pages, $8.00 each added page

Plat or condominium drawing$40.00 per 8 by 14 inch plat

Ohio's standardization statute, R.C. 317.114, took effect on July 1, 2009. It calls for type of ten points or larger, black or blue ink, no highlighting and paper between letter size and 14 inches long. Leave an inch of white space on the sides and the bottom, three inches at the head of the first page and an inch and a half at the head of later ones.

The Recorder will still accept a deed that does not conform, but adds $20.00 to the bill. The statute exempts court and tax authority documents, plats, DD-214 discharges, state and federal papers and anything executed before the effective date. Marginal clutter such as page numbers, initials and bar codes is not charged.

sections.h2: Other records that show up in a sale
sections.html:
Title work on a Gallia County house often turns up more than the deed. These other filings sit in the same indexes:

  • Mechanic's liens and notices of commencement.
  • Federal tax liens and releases, personal property tax liens and workers' compensation liens.
  • Land contracts, powers of attorney and trust documents.
  • A Notice to Medicaid Estate Recovery of Pending Transfer of Property, a form the Recorder links on its fees page.

Run the parcel through the Recorder's search and the Auditor's search before you sign a contract. A lien found after a contract is signed holds up the closing.

Gallia had 29,220 people in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 29,072. Owners hold 74.7 percent of homes, the median value is $155,600, and the median rent is $813 against a median household income of $56,830. Of 13,430 housing units, 13.1 percent were vacant in 2020, and only seven building permits were issued in 2025.

A seller here is often handling an older house in a county where new construction is thin, which makes the title and lien check worth doing early. Gallipolis is the county seat and largest village. A buyer from across the state line in Cabell or Mason County, West Virginia, still records the deed in Gallipolis.

With a cash buyer you skip the lender's timeline, but the same two stops apply: the Auditor's transfer, then the Recorder. Before you go, confirm the legal description against your last deed, check that the notary block shows a seal and expiration date, and enclose a stamped return envelope big enough for the papers. Any of those gaps sends the deed back and costs you days. If you are unsure about a detail, call the Recorder on 740-446-4612 before you make the trip, because the deputies can tell you what a checklist item means even though they cannot fix the document.

faqs.q: What is the first-two-pages recording fee in Gallia County?
faqs.a: The Recorder lists $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after them. The state base is $34, which a county may raise with a preservation surcharge of up to $5.

faqs.q: Which Gallipolis office comes first, the Auditor or the Recorder?
faqs.a: The Auditor. The transfer has to happen there before recording. Both offices are at 18 Locust Street, and the Auditor's real estate desk is on extension 1201.

faqs.q: Can the Recorder correct an error in my legal description?
faqs.a: No. Deputies cannot change lot numbers or other details even when the error looks like a typo. The person who prepared the document has to fix it and sign again.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to record a military discharge in Gallia County?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder records discharge papers and the Honorable Discharge Certificate at no cost, and one certified copy of a service discharge is free.

faqs.q: How do I look up an old Gallia County deed?
faqs.a: Use the Recorder's online records index, or the Auditor's parcel search by owner, parcel or address. The counter at 18 Locust Street runs on weekday hours, eight to four, and browsing the records costs nothing.
